$comment: Commercial catalogue for every sellable product in this repository. Product entries live in packaging/products/*.json and are merged into this file by scripts/packaging/catalog.mjs. Edit the data here; never edit generated output in dist/ or packaging/listings/.

meta.$placeholders: Every value containing REPLACE-ME must be filled in before launch. `npm run pkg:verify` fails while any remain, so the packages cannot be shipped half-configured.

currency.$note: These rates are a starting point entered by hand, not a live feed. Paystack and Selar settle in GHS/NGN, so re-check both before a launch and re-run `npm run pkg:listings`; a stale rate silently changes your margin.

platforms.name: Gumroad
platforms.notes: Gumroad hosts the file and mails the download link itself. Use its Versions feature for the three licences â€” one product, one page, one review count.

platforms.name: Selar
platforms.notes: Built for African sellers: mobile money, bank transfer and card, paid out locally. Selar delivers the file on its own; the webhook in this repo is for mirroring the sale into your own records.

platforms.name: Shopify

title.$note: Shopify allows 255, but titles over ~70 are truncated in search results.

metaDescription.$note: Hard limit 320; 155 is what Google actually shows.

platforms.notes: Shopify does not deliver digital files without help. Either install a digital-downloads app, or point the orders/paid webhook at this repo's /api/webhooks/shopify and let it issue the download link.

platforms.name: Paystack Storefront
platforms.notes: Paystack takes the money but does not host files. Delivery is this repo's /api/webhooks/paystack: charge.success is verified by signature, then the buyer is emailed a download link.

platforms.name: WhatsApp Business

description.$note: Meta commerce catalogues accept far more, but WhatsApp shows roughly the first 200 characters before a 'more' link. Front-load the value.

platforms.notes: No payment API and no automatic delivery. Money arrives by mobile money or transfer, you confirm it, then `npm run pkg:grant` issues the same signed download link the automated platforms use.
